note: HEAD-QA wording adapted by AI (scripts/adapt-headqa.mjs, lib/mcq-adapt.mjs): kept only when a blind examiner chose the published key. hash ties it to the pooled question; refused: the last refusal per question.

headqa-2013-101.stem: A 30-year-old is found to have a serum calcium of 2.74 mmol/L (normal < 2.62 mmol/L) at a routine workplace health check. PTH is 4.8 pmol/L (normal 1.1–5.8 pmol/L). The history is unremarkable, except that the patient's mother and paternal grandfather were diagnosed with hyperparathyroidism and had surgery, but both remained hypercalcaemic. Which test is most useful to confirm the diagnosis?

headqa-2013-106.stem: A 67-year-old patient taking ticlopidine presents to the emergency department with headache, fatigue and petechiae on the lower limbs. Blood tests show haemoglobin 82 g/L, MCV 100 fL, platelets 25 × 10^9/L and white cell count 7.5 × 10^9/L with a normal differential. The reticulocyte count is raised and the blood film shows numerous schistocytes. Coagulation studies (APTT, PT and fibrinogen) are normal. Biochemistry is notable for LDH 2700 U/L and bilirubin 44 µmol/L. What is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2013-110.stem: A 34-year-old man presents with fever and malaise. His history includes sex with a new male partner over the past 4 months. Two months before presentation he had a painless ulcer on the glans with bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy, all of which resolved spontaneously. Serology results: HIV negative, RPR 1:320, TPHA 1:128. What treatment would you give this patient?
options: IV benzylpenicillin (penicillin G) 24 million units daily for 14 days.
IM benzathine benzylpenicillin 2.4 million units weekly for 3 weeks.
IM ceftriaxone 2 g as a single dose.
IM benzathine benzylpenicillin 2.4 million units as a single dose.

headqa-2013-112.stem: A 54-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus presents to the clinic. He reports a fever of 40 °C with chills and rigors, joint and muscle pains and headache, for which he started paracetamol. The illness began 24 hours before he returned to Spain. Three days later he developed a generalised maculopapular rash, which progressed to more marked petechiae on the lower limbs. Blood tests show leucopenia (white cells 3.2 × 10^9/L), platelets 91 × 10^9/L and mildly raised aminotransferases. Thick and thin blood films, malaria polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and malaria antigen tests are negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2013-116.stem: A 17-year-old boy presents to a general practice with 48 hours of fever to 39 °C and a sore throat. His GP checks his records, which show no previous illnesses. He has no cough, and examination shows bilateral white tonsillar exudate and enlarged, tender anterior cervical lymph nodes. What is the treatment of choice for this patient?

headqa-2013-126.stem: A 38-year-old man presents with dyspnoea and haemoptysis. Blood tests show creatinine 619 µmol/L, urea 41.6 mmol/L and high-titre positive anti-GBM (anti-glomerular basement membrane) antibodies. Renal biopsy shows crescents in 75% of glomeruli, and immunofluorescence shows linear immunoglobulin deposition. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: It is IgA nephropathy with acute kidney injury.
Mycophenolate mofetil is the initial treatment of choice.
The glomerular damage is caused by circulating immune complexes.

headqa-2013-130.stem: A 26-year-old patient with no past medical or surgical history presents to the emergency department with 15 days of dyspnoea. Examination is unremarkable apart from a hard nodule in the left testis. Chest X-ray shows multiple 'cannonball' pulmonary nodules. Blood tests are notable for a β-hCG of 30,000 IU/L. What is the most likely origin of this presentation?

headqa-2013-131.stem: A 49-year-old asymptomatic man, whose father died of prostate cancer, has a PSA (prostate-specific antigen) of 5.9 µg/L (5.9 ng/mL) on a routine workplace health check, with a free-to-total PSA ratio of 11%. Digital rectal examination shows increased firmness of the right prostatic lobe. What is the next appropriate step?
options: Arrange a transrectal ultrasound and prostate biopsy.
Start a 5-alpha reductase inhibitor to halve the PSA level.
Start combined treatment with an LHRH analogue and an antiandrogen.

headqa-2013-133.stem: A 55-year-old man with asthma presents to the emergency department with an exacerbation. One hour after supplemental oxygen and two salbutamol nebulisers he has not improved. On examination his respiratory rate is 42 breaths/min, with supraclavicular indrawing and widespread inspiratory and expiratory wheeze. His peak flow has fallen from 310 to 220 L/min. An arterial blood gas on 28% oxygen shows a PaO2 of 7.2 kPa (54 mmHg) and a PaCO2 of 4.7 kPa (35 mmHg). Which of the following measures is LEAST appropriate?
options: Nebulise ipratropium bromide with salbutamol every 20 minutes.

headqa-2013-142.stem: A 65-year-old man with pancreatic cancer who is receiving chemotherapy presents to the emergency department with pain and swelling of the whole lower limb from the groin down. Which diagnostic test is the most cost-effective for confirming the suspected diagnosis?

headqa-2013-147.stem: After a car accident, a 38-year-old patient is admitted to the ICU in a coma. After several days there is no neurological improvement, and CT shows punctate haemorrhagic lesions in the corpus callosum and at the grey–white matter junction. What is the diagnosis?

headqa-2013-149.stem: A 76-year-old man presents with an 8-month history of cognitive decline and slow, clumsy movements. His family report that he has had visual hallucinations, so his general practitioner prescribed low-dose risperidone, after which his motor function worsened markedly. Based on these findings, what is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2013-152.stem: An 80-year-old man is admitted with sudden-onset aphasia and right hemiparesis. His history includes hypertension well controlled with diet, and cognitive decline over the past year that his neurologist is investigating. Emergency CT of the head shows a left frontal lobar haematoma with no contrast enhancement. What is the most likely cause of the haematoma?
options: An arteriovenous malformation hidden by the acute haematoma.
Isolated vasculitis of the central nervous system.

headqa-2013-160.stem: A 70-year-old man with no history of trauma presents with a few months of low back pain and difficulty walking, with weakness and paraesthesia in both legs that force him to stop a few metres after he starts walking. He increasingly leans his trunk forward. What is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2013-169.stem: An 80-year-old woman presents with a 1-month history of progressive abdominal distension. Over the previous 4–5 months she has had fatigue, anorexia and weight loss of unspecified amount. On examination she has tense ascites and ankle oedema, with no other relevant signs. Abdominal ultrasound and CT show ascites of uniform density, with no visible peritoneal deposits and no abdominal or pelvic masses. The liver, pancreas, adrenal glands, spleen and kidneys are unremarkable. Paracentesis with a wide-bore needle yields, with difficulty, a thick, gelatinous, slightly yellowish fluid. What is the most likely cause?
options: Decompensation with ascites due to liver cirrhosis.
Chylous ascites due to non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

headqa-2013-175.stem: A previously healthy infant presents with acute gastroenteritis of one day's duration and signs of mild dehydration. There is no blood or mucus in the stool, and the infant is tolerating oral intake. What is the initial treatment of choice in this setting?
options: IV rehydration, nil by mouth for 8 hours, then start feeding with a binding diet.
Low-osmolarity oral rehydration solution (sodium 60–75 mmol/L) and continue usual diet.
Low-osmolarity ORS (sodium 60–75 mmol/L), usual diet and oral amoxicillin for 10 days.
Low-osmolarity ORS (sodium 60–75 mmol/L) and start feeding with lactose-free formula.
Low-osmolarity ORS (sodium 60–75 mmol/L), usual diet and loperamide for 7 days.

headqa-2013-180.stem: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the general practice clinic. Five minutes earlier he developed facial angioedema, conjunctivitis, nasal congestion and hoarseness after eating a spoonful of yoghurt given to him by mistake at school. He has a known diagnosis of cow's milk protein allergy. On examination he has mild hypotension, a heart rate of 110 beats/min and SpO2 of 93%. He is pale and slightly sweaty, with widespread wheeze. What is the first-line treatment?

headqa-2013-184.stem: A 32-year-old woman seeks preconception advice. She had a cervical cone biopsy for a high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) and has since had three pregnancy losses at 20–22 weeks' gestation. She has no living children. Each time she presented to the Emergency Department with a feeling of heaviness in the lower abdomen and was found to be 8 cm dilated with bulging membranes. She never felt any contractions. What advice would you give her for her next pregnancy?
options: I would recommend prophylactic oral atosiban throughout the pregnancy.
I would offer corticosteroids for fetal lung maturation from 19–20 weeks.
I would recommend an elective cervical cerclage from 14 weeks' gestation.
I would advise against further pregnancies because of the high risk of recurrence.
I would recommend assisted reproductive technology.

headqa-2013-188.stem: A 16-year-old girl presents with primary amenorrhoea. She has normal female development of secondary sexual characteristics. Oestradiol and testosterone levels are normal. Gynaecological examination shows vaginal agenesis. Ultrasound shows an absent uterus, normal-appearing ovaries and no left kidney. What is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2013-220.stem: A 50-year-old woman has had 1 month of low mood, anhedonia, memory loss, tearfulness, loss of energy, feelings of worthlessness and guilt, marked weight loss and early morning waking, and she is unable to do her usual tasks at home. She has been going through a separation for 3 months. What is the most appropriate diagnosis?

headqa-2013-233.stem: A 16-year-old presents with primary amenorrhoea. There is no relevant medical or surgical history. On examination she has female secondary sexual characteristics and female external genitalia, with Tanner stage III–IV breast development and sparse pubic and axillary hair. Her height is on the 90th percentile for her age. A plain X-ray shows a bone age of 15.8 years. Blood tests show an oestradiol of 184 pmol/L (50 pg/mL) and raised gonadotrophins. Which of the following conditions is consistent with these findings?

headqa-2013-42.stem: A 70-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and moderate heart failure presents with a persistent dry cough that began as a tickling sensation in her throat. Blood tests show hyperkalaemia. Which drug is most likely to have caused her symptoms and the blood test abnormality?

headqa-2013-64.stem: A 45-year-old woman with a heart murmur first detected in childhood presents to the Emergency Department with palpitations, easy fatigue and oedema. On examination there is no cyanosis. SpO2 is 97% and BP is 120/80 mmHg. The heart rate is irregular at 100 bpm. There is a grade 2/6 ejection systolic murmur in the pulmonary area and wide, fixed splitting of the second heart sound. There are no crackles. There is mild hepatomegaly (2–3 cm) and mild ankle oedema. ECG: atrial fibrillation at 100 bpm, QRS axis +120° and right bundle branch block. What is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2013-68.stem: A 52-year-old patient presents with a 6-month history of dyspnoea on moderate exertion. There has been no angina or syncope. Physical examination and diagnostic tests show a mean transvalvular aortic gradient of 55 mmHg, a calculated aortic valve area of 0.7 cm² and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 65%. Which treatment should this patient be given?
options: Diuretics and more frequent specialist follow-up.
If exertional dyspnoea worsens, percutaneous balloon dilatation of the aortic valve.
Aortic valve replacement with a mechanical prosthesis or bioprosthesis.
Aortic valve replacement with a homograft.

headqa-2013-78.stem: A 45-year-old man had a truncal vagotomy and antrectomy with Billroth II reconstruction for chronic peptic ulcer disease with pyloroduodenal stenosis. Six weeks after surgery, he reports that shortly after meals (within half an hour) he develops nausea, weakness, sweating, dizziness and abdominal cramps, usually with diarrhoea. What is the most appropriate initial management?
options: A trial of treatment with a benzodiazepine.
Investigation for a probable neuroendocrine tumour (e.g. carcinoid).
Surgery to create an antiperistaltic Roux-en-Y gastrojejunostomy.

headqa-2013-82.stem: A 55-year-old man, whose son has coeliac disease, presents with iron deficiency anaemia and a recent increase in bowel frequency. HLA typing shows he is negative for both the HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8 alleles. Which diagnostic investigation is most appropriate in this case?
options: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with duodenal biopsies.
Assessment of response to a gluten-free diet.

headqa-2013-90.stem: A 50-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with fatigue, anorexia, weight loss, jaundice, fever and abdominal pain. She reports no recent blood transfusion, high-risk sexual contact or injecting drug use. She has drunk 60 g of alcohol a day for 5 years, more over the past month due to family problems. Temperature 38.5°C, BP 100/60 mmHg. She is disoriented to time and place, malnourished, with asterixis, jaundice and tender hepatomegaly; no ascites or peritonism. Bloods: WCC 15 × 10⁹/L (90% neutrophils), RBC 3.0 × 10¹²/L, Hb 100 g/L, MCV 115 fL, bilirubin 257 µmol/L (mainly conjugated), AST 300 U/L, ALT 120 U/L, GGT 635 U/L, prothrombin time prolonged by more than 50%. What is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2013-91.stem: A 17-year-old boy, an athlete with no relevant medical history, sees his doctor for intermittent yellowing of the sclerae. He denies taking any drugs and has no abdominal pain. Blood tests show normal ALT, AST, GGT and alkaline phosphatase, with a total bilirubin of 55 µmol/L and a conjugated (direct) bilirubin of 7 µmol/L. He is not anaemic and an abdominal ultrasound shows a normal liver. What is the diagnosis?

headqa-2013-99.stem: A 45-year-old woman is referred by the surgical team with a neuroendocrine tumour, diagnosed after a partial pancreatectomy for a 2-cm tumour in the tail of the pancreas. The tumour was found incidentally on an abdominal CT scan requested to further investigate a simple liver cyst. On questioning, she reports irregular periods, with amenorrhoea for the past 6 months, and recurrent renal colic since the age of 20, for which she has needed lithotripsy several times. She also has a family history of renal colic. What is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2014-106.stem: A 78-year-old man presents with 3 days of nausea and vomiting. Three weeks ago he had cardiac catheterisation with revascularisation of the right coronary artery. His blood pressure is 185/85 mmHg and there are purple lesions on the toes of both feet. Blood tests show urea 38.3 mmol/L and creatinine 513 µmol/L. What is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2014-110.stem: A 78-year-old man with poorly controlled rheumatoid arthritis (RA) has had 2 admissions in the past 6 months for heart failure and atrial fibrillation. Current medications: infliximab, prednisone, furosemide, enalapril, carvedilol and acenocoumarol. He is readmitted with biventricular heart failure. ECG: atrial fibrillation at 102 bpm and complete left bundle branch block. Echocardiogram: biatrial dilatation, thickened left ventricular wall, ejection fraction 45% and a restrictive filling pattern. Bloods: Hb 100 g/L, creatinine 186 µmol/L (GFR 20 mL/min), CRP 124 mg/L, rheumatoid factor 240 U/L, BNP 980 ng/L; proteinuria 4.8 g/24 h. What is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2014-111.stem: A 40-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a swollen right knee of about 24 hours' duration. He reports no preceding trauma, and this is his first episode of arthritis. On focused history, he returned from a trip to Morocco 4 weeks ago; while there he had chills and diarrhoea, which settled after a week. Examination also reveals inflammation of the right Achilles tendon. What is the most appropriate approach?
options: This is a spondyloarthropathy; start methotrexate.
Immobilise the knee in a bandage for 15 days and give NSAIDs.
Perform arthrocentesis for synovial fluid culture, crystal analysis and cell count.
This is gouty arthritis; start allopurinol.

headqa-2014-115.stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with maculopapular lesions on the upper limbs and no other symptoms. Biopsy of one lesion shows non-caseating granulomas. Blood tests are normal apart from a raised serum angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) level. Chest X-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy. Which of the following is the most appropriate approach?

headqa-2014-119.stem: A 23-year-old man jumps while playing basketball and lands on his right leg with the knee hyperextended, twisting the knee sharply while his foot stays planted on the ground. He feels a pop and sharp knee pain and cannot continue playing. He reports a feeling of instability when bearing weight on that leg. Examination shows a large knee effusion, so arthrocentesis is performed, yielding a large acute haemarthrosis with no fat droplets floating on the aspirated fluid. Knee range of motion is full and Lachman's test is positive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus.
Isolated rupture of the lateral collateral ligament.
Avulsion fracture of the anterior tibial spine.
Unicondylar fracture of the medial condyle.
Rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament.

headqa-2014-124.stem: A 60-year-old patient presents to the hospital emergency department with left-sided chest pain, cough with yellowish sputum, a temperature of 38.7 °C and shortness of breath. Arterial oxygen saturation is 80%. Full blood count: white cell count 12.0 × 10⁹/L with 86% neutrophils. Chest X-ray: alveolar infiltrate at the left base with an air bronchogram. Pneumonia is suspected; a urinary pneumococcal antigen test is positive, and sputum is sent to Microbiology for culture. Which of the following is the most appropriate empirical antibiotic while awaiting microbiology results?

headqa-2014-146.stem: Which of the following clinical scenarios should raise suspicion of a paraneoplastic process and therefore require screening for malignancy?
options: Boy, 13: palpable purpura on legs and buttocks, arthralgia and abdominal pain.
Man, 36: target lesions on back, hands, palms and forearms; oral erosions and ulcers.
Woman, 44: malar and nasal bridge erythema, photosensitivity, fingertip erythema.
Man, 27: symmetric periorificial and acral depigmentation; patchy occipital alopecia
Woman, 68: proximal weakness, violaceous periorbital rash, papules over finger joints

headqa-2014-158.stem: A 28-year-old nulliparous Caucasian woman attends her annual gynaecological check-up and asks about reducing her risk of ovarian cancer, as her mother died of this cancer at age 64. Detailed questioning reveals no other family history of ovarian or breast cancer. Which of the following strategies is most appropriate to reduce this patient's risk of ovarian cancer?
options: Advise formula feeding rather than breastfeeding if she becomes pregnant.

headqa-2014-162.stem: A woman at 31 weeks' gestation presents to the emergency department reporting fluid leaking from the vagina. Speculum examination shows clear fluid coming from the external cervical os. She is afebrile. Cardiotocography shows no contractions and a normal fetal heart rate. Ultrasound shows no fetal malformations and the cervix is not shortened. Which treatment combination would you give?

headqa-2014-163.stem: A 26-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with abdominal pain and light vaginal bleeding. She reports 7 weeks of amenorrhoea. A pregnancy test is positive. What is the next step?
options: Advise rest at home and repeat the pregnancy test in one week.
Evacuate the uterus by suction curettage.
Give standard micronised vaginal progesterone until 14 weeks' gestation.
Evacuate the uterus with vaginal prostaglandins.

headqa-2014-181.stem: You are shown a cohort study of 1000 women who smoke and 2000 non-smoking women of the same age. After 5 years, 30 of the smokers and 20 of the non-smokers have had a stroke. What are the relative risk and the attributable risk?

headqa-2014-183.stem: A study was done to find the risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB) linked to the use of different non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). It included 2,777 patients with UGIB and 5,532 patients matched to them by age and by month of admission or consultation. These matched patients came from the same hospitals and had been admitted or seen for reasons unrelated to NSAID use. The comparative risk of UGIB with previous exposure to each NSAID was then calculated. What type of study is this?

headqa-2014-189.stem: A study looks at the association between factor X and disease Z. It includes 120 people with the disease and 420 controls without the disease, matched for age and sex. In each group, 20 people had been exposed to factor X. What is the odds ratio (OR) for factor X and disease Z?

headqa-2014-198.stem: In a cohort study, severe haemorrhage occurred in 3% of people treated with an anticoagulant and in 1% of untreated people. The number needed to harm (NNH) was 50. How should these results be interpreted?
options: In the anticoagulant group, 50 people had a severe haemorrhage.
The treated group had 50 more severe haemorrhages than the untreated group.
Severe haemorrhage was 50 times more likely in treated than in untreated people.
50 people had to be treated to cause 1 severe haemorrhage attributable to the drug.
Of every 100 patients treated with the anticoagulant, 50 had a severe haemorrhage.

headqa-2014-228.stem: A 58-year-old woman is admitted to the Short Stay Medical Unit. Her illness began with a syncopal episode, followed by dizziness and dyspnoea. On examination she is sweaty and afebrile. Her heart rate is 126 beats/min, respiratory rate 30 breaths/min, blood pressure 88/46 mmHg and oxygen saturation 85% on room air. Heart sounds are tachycardic with no murmurs or gallop, and the chest is clear on auscultation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Acute pulmonary oedema secondary to atrial flutter.

headqa-2014-229.stem: A 69-year-old woman presents with blood-stained sputum. Over the previous two months she had low-grade fever, fatigue, anorexia and weight loss of unknown amount. Sputum cytology showed haemosiderin-laden macrophages, and her chest X-ray showed bilateral alveolar infiltrates. Key blood test results: haemoglobin 82 g/L, PaO2 58 mmHg (7.7 kPa), creatinine 442 µmol/L. Urinalysis showed proteinuria +++, microscopic haematuria and red cell casts. Perinuclear antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (p-ANCA) were positive, anti-glomerular basement membrane antibodies were negative and antinuclear antibodies were negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Systemic lupus erythematosus with severe renal involvement.

headqa-2014-36.stem: A 76-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with right groin pain and vomiting for about 6 hours. On examination there is a hard lump just below the line joining the anterior superior iliac spine and the pubis (the line of the inguinal ligament). What is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2014-43.stem: A 66-year-old man with known alcohol-related liver cirrhosis is brought to the Emergency Department with increasing abdominal girth and disorientation to time and place. On examination he has ascites and asterixis (flapping tremor). Which of the following investigations should be performed urgently?
options: Head CT to rule out a stroke.
Abdominal ultrasound to confirm the presence of ascites.
Diagnostic paracentesis to rule out spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.
Abdominal CT to rule out hepatocellular carcinoma.

headqa-2014-47.stem: A 49-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with rigors, fever of 39°C, right upper quadrant pain, jaundice and vomiting. On examination her blood pressure is 100/50 mmHg and heart rate 110 bpm. She is prostrated, with right upper quadrant tenderness and a positive Murphy's sign. Blood tests show leucocytosis with a left shift, and abdominal ultrasound shows cholelithiasis, choledocholithiasis and dilatation of the extrahepatic bile duct. Empirical antibiotics and IV fluids are started. What is the most effective procedure to perform next?
options: Continue antibiotics and supportive care, followed by elective cholecystectomy later.
Placement of an external biliary drain.
Urgent cholecystectomy with cannulation of the common bile duct.

headqa-2014-48.stem: A 60-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension presents with palpitations over several weeks. She brings an ECG taken a week ago showing atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of 70 bpm. On examination and on a repeat ECG in the clinic she is in sinus rhythm. Does she need long-term anticoagulation?
options: No, because her atrial fibrillation is paroxysmal and she is not currently in it.
No, because she is under 75 years old and has not had a previous stroke.
Yes, long-term anticoagulation is needed: her CHADS2 is 2 and CHA2DS2-VASc is 3.
No anticoagulation is needed, but aspirin antiplatelet therapy may be prescribed.
Only with subcutaneous low molecular weight heparin while in atrial fibrillation.

headqa-2014-49.stem: A 32-year-old man with no relevant medical history or cardiovascular risk factors has had 1 month of dyspnoea on climbing one flight of stairs. He now presents after a sudden syncope preceded by exertion. His brother died suddenly of unexplained causes. On examination there is a harsh systolic murmur, loudest at the aortic area. The ECG shows sinus rhythm with a pattern consistent with left ventricular hypertrophy. Echocardiography shows marked asymmetric hypertrophy of the interventricular septum with a dynamic subvalvular gradient of 70 mmHg, moderate secondary mitral regurgitation and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction. Which of the following treatments is the LEAST indicated?

headqa-2014-50.stem: A 65-year-old man who smokes and has diabetes is brought to the Emergency Department with oppressive chest pain and sweating for about an hour. The ECG shows sinus rhythm at 80 bpm and complete left bundle branch block. What should our management be?
options: Measure troponin and await the result to confirm acute myocardial infarction.
Manage as ST-elevation MI and give reperfusion therapy as early as possible.
Insert a transcutaneous pacemaker in case a more advanced block develops.
Perform an urgent CT scan to rule out acute pulmonary embolism.
Give NSAIDs, as this could be acute pericarditis.

headqa-2014-53.stem: A 55-year-old man with obesity and dyslipidaemia, who currently smokes, is being investigated for resistant hypertension with no evidence so far of cardiac or renal damage. He reports morning headaches and daytime sleepiness. 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring confirms hypertension despite 3 drugs, one of them a diuretic, with night-time blood pressures higher than daytime. Given your clinical suspicion, which diagnostic test would you request next?

headqa-2014-63.stem: A 70-year-old man presents with progressive dyspnoea and a non-productive cough of several years' duration. Chest X-ray shows pleural plaques on the mediastinal and diaphragmatic pleura. CT confirms these plaques and also shows reticulonodular changes predominantly in the lower zones. Which of the following would you recommend first?
options: Order blood tests to rule out eosinophilia.

headqa-2014-70.stem: A 50-year-old male mechanic presents with a two-year history of difficulty using his right hand and a feeling of stiffness in the arm. His wife has noticed his face is expressionless and reports that he has very vivid nightmares that wake him up agitated. On examination there is rigidity in the right limbs, and he walks slowly without swinging his right arm. What is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2014-78.stem: A 45-year-old patient presents to the emergency department with general malaise, headache and progressive tiredness over recent weeks. On examination there is mild jaundice of the skin and mucous membranes, and the spleen is palpable 2 cm below the costal margin. Blood tests show haemoglobin 86 g/L and MCV 100 fL. The reticulocyte count is raised and the blood film shows anisopoikilocytosis. Biochemistry shows LDH 1300 U/L, bilirubin 37.6 µmol/L and undetectable haptoglobin. Which test is most appropriate to guide the diagnosis?
options: Iron studies, vitamin B12 and folate levels.

headqa-2014-79.stem: A 35-year-old woman receiving hormonal treatment for infertility presents to the emergency department with constitutional symptoms and paraesthesia on the left side of her body. Blood tests show Hb 75 g/L, reticulocytes 10% (normal 0.5–2%), platelets 5 × 10^9/L, normal white cell count, LDH 1200 U/L, negative direct Coombs test and undetectable haptoglobin. The peripheral blood film shows abundant schistocytes. Coagulation studies are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis and the most appropriate treatment?
options: Thrombocytopenic purpura. Start corticosteroids and platelet transfusion.
Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura. Treat with plasma exchange.

headqa-2014-80.stem: A 70-year-old man is scheduled for cataract extraction. He has had a mechanical mitral valve prosthesis for 10 years and takes acenocoumarol. His ECG shows sinus rhythm. Which of the following recommendations is most appropriate?
options: Perform the eye surgery without stopping acenocoumarol.
Stop acenocoumarol 5 days before surgery and restart it the day after.
Stop acenocoumarol 5 days before; start LMWH 3 days before; stop LMWH 24 h before.
Stop acenocoumarol 1 day before surgery and give fresh frozen plasma during it.
Stop acenocoumarol 1 day before surgery and give vitamin K just before it.

headqa-2014-85.stem: A 34-year-old woman is admitted to hospital with a pulmonary embolism confirmed on CT pulmonary angiography. She has no history of recent surgery, trauma or travel. She reports Raynaud's phenomenon for 2 years, and the previous year she had a miscarriage at 12 weeks' gestation. There is no family history of venous thromboembolism. The activated partial thromboplastin time is 56 s (normal 25–35 s) and the platelet count is 120 × 10^9/L. Which of the following tests would be most helpful in making the diagnosis?

headqa-2014-91.stem: A 25-year-old man with no relevant personal or family history is admitted to neurosurgery with a skull fracture after a motorcycle accident. Three days later he develops abrupt-onset polyuria, polydipsia and intense thirst, both day and night. Investigations show a urine output of 7 L, urine osmolality 190 mOsm/kg (90–1200) and plasma osmolality 292 mOsm/kg (275–295). Plasma sodium is 143 mmol/L. A water deprivation test is performed and, after confirming that urine osmolality does not rise, 2 micrograms of desmopressin is given subcutaneously. Urine osmolality afterwards is 410 mOsm/kg. What is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2014-95.stem: A 33-year-old woman has lost 6 kg over the past 4 months, with fatigue and anorexia, and has had amenorrhoea for 2 months. Hormone tests show a basal serum cortisol of 108 nmol/L (normal basal range 115–550 nmol/L), rising to 123 nmol/L after ACTH stimulation. Basal plasma ACTH is 48 pmol/L (normal 2–12 pmol/L). What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Tertiary adrenal insufficiency due to a hypothalamic lesion.
Further tests are needed as the diagnosis is inconclusive.

headqa-2014-99.stem: A 47-year-old man presents with lower limb oedema of 3 weeks' duration. Blood tests show creatinine 115 µmol/L, total cholesterol 6.98 mmol/L and albumin 24 g/L. Urine microscopy shows 15–20 red cells per high-power field, and a 24-hour urine collection shows proteinuria of 3.7 g/day. What is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2015-104.stem: A 46-year-old man who injects drugs presents to the emergency department with a 24-hour history of fever with rigors, confusion, diffuse myalgia and severe pain in the left hand, without obvious local signs of inflammation. He reports no history of trauma. On examination: temperature 38.9°C, heart rate 120/min, respiratory rate 30/min, blood pressure 90/54 mmHg. Blood tests show leucocytosis with a left shift (white cell count 25 × 10^9/L, 80% neutrophils), raised creatinine (141 µmol/L) and CK 138 U/L. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2015-105.stem: A 65-year-old patient with no relevant medical history presents to the emergency department with a fever of 39 °C, meningism and signs of severe illness (coma, BP 80/60 mmHg, poor peripheral perfusion). Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action at this point?
options: Blood cultures, fluids, IV dexamethasone+ceftriaxone+vancomycin+ampicillin, then CT, LP
Urgent CT, fundoscopy, then CSF culture and antibiotics guided by CSF Gram stain
IV antipyretic, high-dose IV dopamine; once stable, CT, LP, CSF-guided antibiotics

headqa-2015-106.stem: A 32-year-old man from Cameroon presents with a 1-month history of fever, cough and left-sided chest pain. A week of amoxicillin-clavulanate did not improve his symptoms. Blood tests show a white cell count of 8.0 × 10^9/L and haemoglobin of 128 g/L. Chest X-ray shows a loculated left pleural effusion occupying one-third of the hemithorax. Thoracentesis yields yellowish fluid with: red cells 2.0 × 10^9/L, white cells 2.5 × 10^9/L (90% lymphocytes), protein 49 g/L, lactate dehydrogenase 550 U/L, glucose 3.7 mmol/L, and no malignant cells on cytology. Which of the following tests would be most useful in diagnosing the cause of the pleural effusion?

headqa-2015-119.stem: A 38-year-old non-smoking woman with known allergic rhinitis presents with a two-month history of cough and intermittent wheeze, mainly at night. Chest X-ray is normal. Spirometry is within normal limits with a negative bronchodilator response. Which of the following tests would you request next?

headqa-2015-138.stem: A 37-year-old man presents with arthritis of the metacarpophalangeal joints of both hands and right-sided pleurisy. Examination shows a bilateral malar rash. Antinuclear antibodies are positive (titre 1:640), anti-double-stranded DNA antibodies are also positive, and anti-Sm antibodies are negative. What would be the initial treatment of choice for this patient?
options: The condition will probably be self-limiting and does not require treatment.

headqa-2015-139.stem: A 70-year-old woman with a history of anorexia, weight loss, aching in the proximal muscles and joints, and pain in the temporomandibular region presents to the emergency department with sudden, painless loss of vision in one eye (hand movements only) and a relative afferent pupillary defect. Which test would you request first to make the diagnosis?

headqa-2015-144.stem: A 50-year-old man attends a scheduled review. He was diagnosed with granulomatosis with polyangiitis 10 years ago, has been off treatment for 5 years and is asymptomatic. Chest X-ray, blood tests and urine sediment are normal, except that antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) are positive at a titre of 1:320 with anti-proteinase 3 specificity, having previously become negative. What is the most appropriate management?

headqa-2015-161.stem: A 27-year-old woman is referred to the gynaecology clinic with an 8-month history of dyspareunia, plus occasional dyschezia and rectal bleeding coinciding with menstruation for the past 3–4 months. She has also had dysmenorrhoea for years, well controlled with ibuprofen. She has been trying to conceive for about 16 months without success. On gynaecological examination, the only finding is tenderness on pressing the posterior vaginal fornix. Which investigation would allow a definitive diagnosis of her condition?

headqa-2015-170.stem: An 80-year-old man attends for assessment before a planned laparoscopic cholecystectomy. He has had treated hypertension for 10 years and denies heart or lung disease. He has no chest pain. He leads an active life and goes to the gym daily, alternating swimming and treadmill walking for at least an hour. Usual medications: nebivolol 5 mg once daily and hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily. Examination: weight 73 kg, height 179 cm, blood pressure 138/80 mmHg, heart rate 60 beats/min. No murmurs are heard. Which of the following is the most appropriate preoperative approach?

headqa-2015-175.stem: An 88-year-old man presents to the clinic after 3 falls in the last 6 months. None of the falls was accompanied by dizziness or syncope. One occurred while he was walking in the garden; on another occasion he tripped inside the house. His history includes hypertension without postural blood pressure changes, gout, osteoarthritis and depression. He takes 5 medications regularly. Which of the following is most likely to be contributing to his falls?

headqa-2015-176.stem: A 78-year-old woman has type 2 diabetes treated with oral hypoglycaemics, hypertension treated with a beta-blocker and an ACE inhibitor, and NYHA class I congestive heart failure (LVEF 48%); she is currently asymptomatic. ECOG performance status 0. She has a 2-year history of small lumps in the neck. Cervical lymph node biopsy: grade 2 follicular lymphoma. Staging: Hb 120 g/L, WCC 6.9 × 10⁹/L (neutrophils 60%, lymphocytes 27%, monocytes 6%, eosinophils 4%, basophils 4%), platelets 220 × 10⁹/L. Bone marrow: infiltrated by follicular lymphoma. Creatinine 133 µmol/L, LDH 235 U/L, beta-2 microglobulin 2.1 mg/L. CT: lymph nodes smaller than 3 cm in the cervical, axillary, retroperitoneal, iliac and inguinal regions; liver and spleen normal. Which of the following treatments is most appropriate?
options: No treatment for now; watch and wait.

headqa-2015-177.stem: A 57-year-old man was diagnosed with stage T3N1M0 colon adenocarcinoma. He was treated with resection followed by six months of adjuvant FOLFOX chemotherapy (fluorouracil, folinic acid and oxaliplatin). At routine follow-up two years later, his carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) has risen to 30 µg/L (previously below 2 µg/L). He is asymptomatic, physical examination is unremarkable and chest X-ray is normal. CT shows a 3 cm mass in the right lobe of the liver, which is avid on PET. No other abnormalities are seen on CT or PET. What is the most appropriate management?
options: FOLFIRI chemotherapy (fluorouracil, folinic acid, irinotecan) plus bevacizumab.
Surgical assessment for resection of the liver lesion.

headqa-2015-188.stem: Police bring in an 80-year-old man found lost at night, blocks from home. He says he feels fine and got lost walking. Systems review unremarkable. He can't recall his medicines; records list glipizide, atenolol, acenocoumarol. 3 ED visits in 3 months: dizziness, back pain, INR 5.0. Reports ADL/IADL independence. No known relatives/friends; refuses social, medical and nursing help. T 37.7°C, BMI 16 kg/m², BP 160/90, HR 90, SpO2 99%; global muscle loss; in a dressing gown, smelling of urine. Refuses the MMSE. WCC 13×10⁹/L, glucose 16.7 mmol/L, HbA1c 11%, INR 0.9. Urine: >50 WBC/HPF, nitrites+, culture >10⁵ CFU/mL gram-negative bacilli. Stable after inpatient antibiotics, insulin and restarted acenocoumarol, he wants to go home; nurses say he can't self-inject insulin. What is the next step in assessing his safety at home?
options: Refer to primary care and local social work to assess safety at home.
Formal assessment of his capacity to make decisions about his health.

headqa-2015-192.stem: An epidemiological study attempted to correlate per capita consumption of processed meat in different countries in 2012 with the incidence of colon cancer recorded in those same countries in the same year. What type of study is this?

headqa-2015-193.stem: A random sample is selected from patients attending a health centre for influenza vaccination during the annual campaign. Among other data, it is recorded whether each selected patient is taking lipid-lowering drugs and whether they have been diagnosed with diabetes mellitus. Diabetes mellitus is found to be more common among patients taking lipid-lowering drugs than among those not taking them. Which of the following describes the design of this study?

headqa-2015-213.stem: Gustavo presents to the emergency department with skin lesions and general malaise of several days' duration. He has psoriasiform lesions on the trunk, with involvement of the palms and soles. He also has asymmetric non-suppurative joint inflammation, bilateral red eyes and erosions on the glans. On further history, he reports a high-risk sexual contact 20 days earlier. What is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2015-217.stem: An 84-year-old woman presents with a 4-day history of vision loss in the left eye accompanied by metamorphopsia. The macula shows abundant hard exudates, two small deep haemorrhages and a localised detachment of the neurosensory retina. The other eye has abundant soft drusen. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2015-226.stem: As part of a bowel cancer screening program, a 52-year-old patient has a colonoscopy. The whole colon looks normal apart from a 2 cm pedunculated polyp in the sigmoid colon, which is removed with a diathermy snare. Histopathology shows carcinoma in situ confined to the head of the polyp. A CT scan of the chest and abdomen is reported as normal. What is the correct management?
options: Segmental resection of the affected colon.
Local resection of the base of the polyp.

headqa-2015-32.stem: A 59-year-old woman presents with a 4-month history of chronic watery diarrhoea. At endoscopy the mucosa shows nothing of note; in particular, there are no ulcers or friable areas. A biopsy of the transverse colon is taken. Histopathology shows a thickened band beneath the surface epithelium, more obvious on Masson's trichrome stain, with associated epithelial atrophy and denudation. There is also a clear increase in intraepithelial lymphocytes. What is the diagnosis of the intestinal lesion?

headqa-2015-50.stem: A 58-year-old man reports a 3-week history of progressive, moderately painful skin lesions on his left arm. They began as an erythematous lesion on his left thumb. Red streaks are visible as lines connecting the lesions. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. He has been working in his garden but cannot recall any injury. The causative organism was identified by culture of a skin biopsy. What is the most likely causative agent?
options: Skin infection due to Staphylococcus aureus.
Skin infection due to Mycobacterium marinum.

headqa-2015-56.stem: A 54-year-old patient is admitted with a measured fever of 38°C over the previous five days and dyspnoea at rest (NYHA class IV) that began 6 hours before presentation. In the emergency department, the examination is consistent with heart failure and the ECG shows complete heart block with a ventricular escape rate of 45 bpm. The heart failure is refractory to medical treatment. Transoesophageal echocardiography shows aortic regurgitation with an effective regurgitant orifice area of 0.5 cm². Serial blood cultures grow Streptococcus gallolyticus. What is the most appropriate management?
options: Mechanical aortic valve replacement plus antibiotics guided by susceptibility testing.
Targeted antibiotics, IABP and temporary pacing for 3 weeks, then permanent pacemaker.
Temporary pacing, targeted antibiotics and transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
Urgent permanent pacemaker plus 6 weeks of targeted antibiotics.

headqa-2015-57.stem: A 72-year-old woman presents to hospital with 2 hours of crushing chest pain. Her blood pressure is 68/32 mmHg, heart rate 124 beats/min, respiratory rate 32 breaths/min and oxygen saturation 91% on 50% oxygen. Chest auscultation reveals bilateral crackles. The ECG shows anterior ST elevation with reciprocal ST depression in the inferior leads. The chest X-ray shows a bilateral alveolar pattern. What is your management?

headqa-2015-71.stem: An 18-year-old with a history of asthma and allergy to pollens, dust mites and cat dander presents to the emergency department with a sensation of food stuck behind the sternum and is almost unable to swallow his own saliva. He reports similar previous episodes that resolved spontaneously within a few minutes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2015-74.stem: A 67-year-old man with liver cirrhosis who is still drinking alcohol is admitted with two weeks of progressive abdominal distension and diffuse discomfort. He reports no fever or other symptoms. On examination there is shifting dullness on abdominal percussion and no oedema. Diagnostic paracentesis yields slightly cloudy fluid with 2,300 cells/mm³, of which 30% are lymphocytes, 60% polymorphonuclear cells and 10% red blood cells. What is the first treatment this patient should receive immediately?

headqa-2015-81.stem: A 30-year-old woman presents with anxiety, weight loss of about 6 kg and a feeling of 'nervousness' over the last three months. Examination shows tachycardia, hyperreflexia and no goitre. Blood tests show TSH <0.01 mU/L, raised T4 and low thyroglobulin. Thyroid scintigraphy shows no uptake in the thyroid region. What is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2015-83.stem: A 49-year-old man presents with marked polyuria and polydipsia and unintentional weight loss of 10 kg. He is diagnosed with diabetes mellitus on the basis of a plasma glucose of 17.9 mmol/L and an HbA1c of 9.8% (84 mmol/mol). His doctor gives dietary advice, recommends physical exercise, and starts metformin 850 mg twice daily and glimepiride 6 mg daily. Over the following weeks his blood glucose readings fall progressively. At 4 months his plasma glucose is 5.2 mmol/L and his HbA1c is 5.9% (41 mmol/mol). He reports frequent episodes of dizziness, epigastric pain, blurred vision, sweating and tremor, which improve when he eats and which occur mainly in the late morning and late afternoon. What change to his treatment would you recommend?
options: Review how carbohydrates are distributed in his diet.
Replace metformin with a DPP-4 inhibitor.

headqa-2015-86.stem: A 31-year-old man is referred from ophthalmology with loss of vision and worsening headache. Examination shows a temporal hemianopia, and pituitary MRI shows a 35 × 30 × 20 mm tumour compressing the optic chiasm and cavernous sinus. Pituitary function tests: cortisol 386 nmol/L, TSH 1.4 mIU/L, free T4 15.4 pmol/L, prolactin 480 µg/L (normal <15), testosterone 5.5 nmol/L (normal 10.4–41.6), FSH 1.2 IU/L (normal 5–15) and LH 2 IU/L (normal 3–15). What is the initial treatment?

headqa-2015-93.stem: A 46-year-old woman with rheumatic valve disease needs mitral valve replacement with a mechanical prosthesis. Her early postoperative course is uneventful. However, after she starts acenocoumarol (a vitamin K antagonist), she develops skin necrosis affecting the abdomen and limbs. Which of the following abnormalities would explain this presentation?

headqa-2016-107.stem: One of the following tick-borne pathogens can be mistaken for malaria, both because of its usual clinical features, which include fever and haemolysis, and because of its appearance on microscopy of Giemsa-stained blood smears. Which pathogen is being described?

headqa-2016-117.stem: A phase III study aims to confirm the bacteriological efficacy of a new antibiotic for treating patients with severe acute pyelonephritis. Which of the following clinical trial designs is most appropriate?
options: Parallel, randomised, double-blind, controlled against another antibiotic.
Crossover, open-label, controlled against another antibiotic.

headqa-2016-131.stem: Researchers want to measure the strength of the association between metabolic syndrome and vitamin D deficiency in the general population. They select a sample of patients older than 18 years from a general practice clinic and book them for a visit. At the visit, each patient is examined to see whether they meet the criteria for metabolic syndrome, and blood is taken to measure serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D. What is the design of this study?

headqa-2016-133.stem: Which of the following study types would be the design of choice to investigate an association between taking a particular drug and a very rare, delayed, serious adverse reaction?
options: Clinical trial of the suspected drug.

headqa-2016-134.stem: A cohort study compares a group of people with hypertension and a group with normal blood pressure. The annual incidence of acute myocardial infarction is 15 per 1000 and 5 per 1000 respectively. Assuming there is no bias or confounding, what is the risk of acute myocardial infarction attributable to hypertension among the hypertensive people?

headqa-2016-140.stem: A 72-year-old presented to the emergency department one month ago after an accidental fall with knee trauma. They now re-present with one week of bilateral lumbar pain and dark urine. History: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidaemia, obesity and knee osteoarthritis. Medications: enalapril/hydrochlorothiazide 20/12.5 mg daily, naproxen as needed, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, metformin 850 mg daily. Bloods: moderate microcytic anaemia, uric acid 565 µmol/L, CK 45 U/L, creatinine 168 µmol/L, urea 12.5 mmol/L, Na 138 mmol/L, K 5.6 mmol/L. Urine: microscopic haematuria ++, protein negative, very abundant desquamated cells, no bacteria. All parameters were normal at the visit one month ago. Urgent ultrasound reports possible bilateral papillary necrosis. What is the most likely current diagnosis?
options: Acute kidney injury due to enalapril.

headqa-2016-156.stem: A 15-year-old boy sees a neurologist, reporting several months of morning jerks in both arms without impaired consciousness. His parents also report almost daily episodes of unresponsiveness with a fixed stare and oral automatisms. In recent days he had a generalised tonic-clonic seizure in the setting of sleep deprivation and alcohol intake. There is a family history of a similar condition. Which of the following would you suspect first?

headqa-2016-162.stem: A 43-year-old woman has a 4 cm intramural uterine fibroid diagnosed on ultrasound. She has two children. Her periods last 4–5 days every 28–30 days and are somewhat heavy, without clots or pain. She has no other symptoms. What would you recommend?

headqa-2016-163.stem: A 31-year-old woman presents with a 2-year history of heavy periods lasting 5 days. Her last period was 8 days ago. On initial assessment, transvaginal ultrasound shows a 25 mm rounded, well-defined, homogeneous, hypoechoic lesion in the endometrial cavity. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: Start a combined oral oestrogen–progestogen with clinical follow-up.
Start tranexamic acid during menses with clinical follow-up.

headqa-2016-168.stem: A pregnant woman at 32 weeks' gestation presents to the emergency department with vaginal bleeding. She has no record of antenatal care but reports a previous caesarean delivery. On speculum examination, red blood is seen coming through the external cervical os. She reports no abdominal pain. CTG confirms no contractions and a normal fetal heart rate. Full blood count is normal. What is the next step?

headqa-2016-171.stem: A 48-year-old woman has a cluster of suspicious microcalcifications detected on screening mammography in the upper outer quadrant of the right breast. Prone vacuum-assisted percutaneous biopsy shows grade II ductal carcinoma in situ. You perform surgical excision of the lesion with radiological hookwire localisation. Histopathology of the specimen shows a 6 mm invasive ductal carcinoma (ER ++ 100%, PR ++ 100%, Ki-67 10%, HER2 negative) with an associated in situ component. Surgical margins are clear. You inform the patient of the result. What would you propose?
options: Chemotherapy + radiotherapy + hormonal therapy with tamoxifen.

headqa-2016-174.stem: A 9-year-old boy presents with fatigue and progressive exertional dyspnoea. A heart murmur was detected at birth, but he was never followed up. On examination, his face and hands are pink, while his lower limbs are cyanosed. Which abnormality would explain these findings?
options: Ventricular septal defect with pulmonary hypertension.
Patent ductus arteriosus with Eisenmenger syndrome.

headqa-2016-181.stem: A 2-month-old girl is referred to the paediatric urology clinic with grade III bilateral vesicoureteric reflux. History: prenatal diagnosis of bilateral renal pelvis dilatation; acute pyelonephritis one month after the diagnostic micturating cystourethrogram. Which of the following is the most advisable?
options: Do nothing, as the reflux may resolve spontaneously.
Request a renal DMSA scan and perform monthly urine cultures.
Antibiotic prophylaxis with amoxicillin and request a renal DMSA scan.

headqa-2016-191.stem: A 60-year-old man with diabetes was admitted to hospital 2 weeks ago with a hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state. He now presents to the Emergency Department with pain and swelling of the right knee. On examination: temperature 37.2°C, heart rate 100 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, and signs of arthritis in the affected joint. Blood tests: white cell count 18 × 10⁹/L, uric acid 482 µmol/L, creatinine 124 µmol/L. Synovial fluid: white cell count 20 × 10⁹/L with 85% neutrophils; no crystals are seen and the Gram stain shows no organisms. What is the most appropriate management?
options: Intra-articular injection of triamcinolone into the affected joint.
Start outpatient amoxicillin–clavulanate and review the response in one week.
Admit and start IV antibiotics immediately while awaiting the culture result.

headqa-2016-192.stem: A 38-year-old man presents with a 2-week history of red, painful nodules over the shins of both legs. He also reports recurrent oral and genital ulcers over the past few months. What is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2016-203.stem: A 50-year-old patient with a history of gout and long-term corticosteroid use is brought to the Emergency Department unable to walk because he cannot extend his knee. X-ray shows a low-lying patella compared with the other knee. What is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2016-213.stem: A 59-year-old man who currently smokes, with a history of hypertension, dyslipidaemia and alcohol use disorder, reports 2 years of progressive difficulty climbing stairs, with weakness of the legs and arms that fluctuates during the day and improves slightly with sustained exercise. He has had occasional episodes of diplopia. Recently he has also developed a persistent dry cough. Electromyography shows an incremental increase in the muscle action potential with repetitive nerve stimulation. Chest CT shows subcarinal lymphadenopathy and a 3.1 cm nodule in the left lower lobe, consistent with primary lung cancer. What is the diagnosis of the associated condition?

headqa-2016-225.stem: An ambulance with a doctor on board is sent to a young man injured in a road traffic crash. On examination he has right-sided anisocoria with a fixed, dilated pupil and is comatose with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 4 (eyes 1, motor 2, verbal 1). Blood pressure is 180/100 mmHg, heart rate 56 beats/min, respiratory rate 8 breaths/min and oxygen saturation 90% on room air. What should the prehospital team do first?
options: Insert a peripheral IV cannula and give IV mannitol.
Endotracheal intubation with cervical spine protection.
Oxygen via Venturi mask and urgent transfer to a hospital with on-call neurosurgery.

headqa-2016-230.stem: A 46-year-old man presents urgently with colicky pain in the left iliac fossa radiating towards the scrotum. He has had no similar episodes before. Blood tests: serum creatinine 80 µmol/L, white cell count 6.7 × 10⁹/L with a normal differential. Urine microscopy shows 12–15 red blood cells per high-power field and urine pH is 6. He is afebrile and his body mass index (BMI) is 25.5 kg/m². Which imaging test is the most sensitive for making the diagnosis?

headqa-2016-232.stem: A 10-year-old girl presents with fatigue, abdominal pain and macroscopic haematuria with dark urine, without urinary symptoms. She has been taking amoxicillin for 3 days for acute tonsillopharyngitis. Her family reports two similar previous self-limiting episodes, which occurred with gastroenteritis and otitis media respectively. What is the most likely diagnosis?

headqa-2016-34.stem: A 41-year-old woman with no relevant medical history presents with exertional dyspnoea that began six months ago and has progressively worsened. Auscultation reveals basal crackles, and the chest X-ray shows bilateral basal opacities. An open lung biopsy is performed. Histopathology shows a complex, heterogeneous lesion in which abnormal areas alternate with preserved areas, with fibrosis of the alveolar septa, prominent fibroblastic foci and type 2 pneumocyte hyperplasia. Involvement is predominantly subpleural. What is the diagnosis of this lung injury?

headqa-2016-37.stem: A genetic polymorphism of the enzyme thiopurine methyltransferase is associated with a high risk of severe haematological toxicity when one of the following drugs is given to homozygous individuals. Which drug is it?

headqa-2016-44.stem: When does left ventricular coronary blood flow reach its maximum?
options: At the beginning of isovolumetric contraction.
When aortic pressure is at its maximum.
When aortic blood flow is at its maximum.

headqa-2016-53.stem: An 80-year-old nursing home resident has urosepsis that is not responding to empirical treatment with ceftriaxone. Blood and urine cultures grow cephalosporin-resistant E. coli, and the laboratory reports that the strain produces extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBL). Which of the following antibiotics should be used?

headqa-2016-62.stem: A 47-year-old man with no significant medical history was diagnosed with hypertension a year ago. He takes amlodipine 10 mg once daily in the morning and losartan/hydrochlorothiazide 100/25 mg once daily in the morning, and follows a low-sodium diet, with good adherence. Despite this, his blood pressure is 168/92 mmHg. What is the next step?
options: Increase the dose of one of his current medications.
Investigate to rule out secondary hypertension.

headqa-2016-74.stem: A 55-year-old patient with a 15-year history of ulcerative colitis undergoes surveillance colonoscopy, which shows a rectal cancer 8 cm from the anal verge and moderately active colitis, mainly in the left colon. After imaging, the tumour is staged as T2N0M0. What is the correct surgical treatment?
options: Panproctocolectomy with ileal pouch–anal anastomosis and defunctioning ileostomy.
Anterior resection of the rectum with defunctioning loop ileostomy.
External beam radiotherapy, then local excision if good response; continue IBD therapy.

headqa-2016-86.stem: A 61-year-old woman with hypertension and atrial fibrillation is followed up in the endocrinology clinic for a multinodular goitre with multiple nodules of 2.5–3 cm in both lobes, none with suspicious features on imaging. At her latest review, 6 months later, she reports dysphagia to solids. Blood tests show TSH 0.001 mIU/L (0.47–4.68) and free T4 20.8 pmol/L (10.0–28.2). Follow-up ultrasound shows a large multinodular goitre with an intrathoracic component and multiple nodules, one of which has grown from 3 to 4.4 cm since the previous scan a year ago. Fine-needle aspiration of this nodule is performed, and cytology is consistent with colloid goitre (benign). What is the most appropriate management?
options: Annual follow-up with thyroid ultrasound and thyroid function tests.

headqa-2016-91.stem: A 33-year-old man is referred from the gastroenterology clinic. He has been diagnosed with hypergastrinaemia secondary to a pancreatic islet cell tumour, and his serum calcium is 3.07 mmol/L (normal 2.12–2.62). What is the most likely diagnosis?
